origins.section: 3.1. A Field's Format Is All the Receiver Has to Find Where It Ends
3.2. A Short Value Is Padded, a Long One Is Refused, and Nothing Else Is Checked
3.3. The Packager Decides the Bytes, So Both Peers Need the Same One
3.4. A Field's Type Decides How You Read Its Value
3.5. Which Fields Must Be Present Depends on the MTI and the Network

gates.says: all 5 of this quiz's answerable readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-error-names-a-later-field: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-error-names-a-later-field: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-error-names-a-later-field: Section 3.1 decides b: the host took 40 characters for DE 43, including the length prefix and the name, so it misread the later fields and the error named a later field written correctly.
recorded.prompt:q-dot-in-an-amount: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-dot-in-an-amount: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-dot-in-an-amount: Section 3.2 decides c: 123.45 came back as 000000123.45 and length is all jPOS checks, so 12.50 is padded to 000000012.50 with the dot kept.
recorded.prompt:q-bcd-prefix: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-bcd-prefix: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-bcd-prefix: Section 3.3 decides a: the BCD prefix counts digits and two digits share a byte, with a filler half-byte for an odd count, so 15 digits fill 8 bytes.
recorded.prompt:q-track-separator: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-track-separator: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-track-separator: Section 3.4 decides c: a D character is packed as the digit 4, so the separator is gone, as the output line shows.
recorded.prompt:q-one-list-of-required-fields: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-one-list-of-required-fields: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-one-list-of-required-fields: Section 3.5 decides a: an 0800 echo test carries no PAN and no amount, only DE 7, DE 11 and DE 70, so a check requiring DE 2 and DE 4 rejects it.

gates.says: all 15 of this quiz's discriminating readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-error-names-a-later-field:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-error-names-a-later-field:a: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-error-names-a-later-field:a: Section 3.1 refutes it: DE 60 was unchanged and the host looked for its length in the wrong place.
recorded.prompt:q-error-names-a-later-field:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-error-names-a-later-field:c: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-error-names-a-later-field:c: Section 3.1 refutes it: the gateway did not touch the later field, which was written correctly.
recorded.prompt:q-error-names-a-later-field:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-error-names-a-later-field:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-error-names-a-later-field:d: Section 3.1 refutes it: the host took a fixed 40 characters for DE 43 and did not stop at the end of the name.
recorded.prompt:q-dot-in-an-amount:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-dot-in-an-amount:a: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-dot-in-an-amount:a: Section 3.2 refutes it: 123.45 went into the ASCII numeric field dot and all.
recorded.prompt:q-dot-in-an-amount:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-dot-in-an-amount:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-dot-in-an-amount:b: Section 3.2 refutes it: a short numeric value is padded with zeros on the left; only a value that is too long is refused.
recorded.prompt:q-dot-in-an-amount:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-dot-in-an-amount:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-dot-in-an-amount:d: Section 3.2 refutes it: the output 000000123.45 shows the dot is kept.
recorded.prompt:q-bcd-prefix:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-bcd-prefix:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-bcd-prefix:b: Section 3.3 refutes it: the BCD prefix counts digits, not bytes.
recorded.prompt:q-bcd-prefix:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-bcd-prefix:c: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-bcd-prefix:c: Section 3.3 refutes it: BCD packs two digits into a byte; one byte per digit is ASCII and EBCDIC.
recorded.prompt:q-bcd-prefix:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-bcd-prefix:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-bcd-prefix:d: Section 3.3 refutes both parts: the prefix counts digits and the digits are packed two to a byte.
recorded.prompt:q-track-separator:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-track-separator:a: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-track-separator:a: Section 3.4 refutes it: a D set in the message comes back as 4, not D.
recorded.prompt:q-track-separator:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-track-separator:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-track-separator:b: Section 3.4 refutes it: only = is turned into the half-byte D and back.
recorded.prompt:q-track-separator:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-track-separator:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-track-separator:d: Section 3.4 refutes it: the issuer receives 24 digits from a 24-character track, so nothing is dropped.
recorded.prompt:q-one-list-of-required-fields:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-one-list-of-required-fields:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-one-list-of-required-fields:b: Section 3.5 refutes it: the echo carries DE 11, and DE 70 is the network management code.
recorded.prompt:q-one-list-of-required-fields:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-one-list-of-required-fields:c: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-one-list-of-required-fields:c: Section 3.5 refutes it: the echo carries no PAN and no amount at all, not zero values.
recorded.prompt:q-one-list-of-required-fields:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-one-list-of-required-fields:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-one-list-of-required-fields:d: Section 3.5 refutes it: getString returns null for an absent field.
